title: Hampton never leaving the bandstand
summary: Hampton's endless encores, stagehands, and the Paris Olympia crew.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yes indeed. But I don't think he can do it now because he can do it. But man, look, we would play a two hour concert and he would do two hours of encores. He couldn't get him off the stand. The only person who could get him off the stand sometimes was his wife. Now Lionel put them vibes down, put those mallets down, come on, go home. The fellow's tired. I just want to play one more tune, baby, I want to play one more tune. And as long as he hear that, he's not going to stop playing. And then sometimes, well he knows how to milk an audience, you know, like he'll play. And we'll play it about a half hour over. Then he'll stop the band and the band would leave, like they're going. And we'd get behind and say, no, no, don't go no way. And when people are halfway out of the place, he starts playing music again, and people start running for his seat and can't find the right seat. And it's just a lot of confusion, you know. But he's that type of guy, man. He likes to do it. As long as he hears that, you can't stop him from playing. Like at some of the theater in Detroit, I mean in New York, the state, what's the name of the big theater in New York, where the stage goes down into the floor? No.

Apollo? No, no, it wasn't Apollo. We played Apollo a lot, but the stage didn't go down. It was down on Seventh Avenue. And he was playing, playing, playing, and they couldn't get him off the stage, so the stage hands just pressed a button. The whole bandstand went down. And it was mad because, and when we played at the Olympic Theater in Paris, there were those guys over there strictly in Union, you know, the stage hands. And those guys, the first night we played there, he got the whole crew fired. Because the crew drew the curtains on him. He had played about fifteen minutes over, and he was going to play some more, so the guy pressed the button, the curtain closed. Oh, he took that for an insult. But most of the time when I left his band, that was the reason. He stayed on the bandstand too long. Too long.
